Methods and sources

How the dataset was counted, how the sample was drawn, and how to read the charts.

↓ Download summary data
DATA PROVENANCE

Historical RockYou corpus

The project uses the password-only, occurrence-count edition distributed by SecLists. The source dates to the 2009 RockYou breach. Each entry pairs a password with its published frequency.

View the dataset source ↗

ANALYSIS DESIGN

A census and a sample

All parsed rows contribute to the structural census. Each row can be counted once or weighted by its published breach occurrence count.

A deterministic uniform reservoir sample of source rows is scored with Python zxcvbn. Score, dictionary, and leetspeak panels describe that sample only; they always count sample rows without occurrence weighting.

Length, character group, and structure filters apply to the census and to matching sample rows. A tiny filtered sample is not representative enough for strong conclusions.

Very long inputs above 72 characters remain in the structural census and are excluded from model scoring. Lengths of 41 or more share an overflow bucket.

FEATURE DICTIONARY

What the labels mean

Character composition
Digits only, letters only, letters + digits, or includes symbols. Unicode character predicates are used; whitespace counts as a symbol. Empty strings share the symbols group and are counted separately in provenance.
Keyboard / sequence
A substring of at least four consecutive characters in selected keyboard rows, the alphabet, number sequences, or their reverse. A heuristic, not exhaustive keyboard geometry.
Repeated block
A block of 1–4 characters repeated at least three times consecutively.
Letters + numeric suffix
At least three ASCII letters followed by 1–6 digits, optionally ending in one listed symbol. The letters can form any string.
Label precedence
Keyboard / sequence → repeated block → letters + numeric suffix → other structure. Groups are mutually exclusive; a password can have further unlabelled features.
Dictionary & leetspeak
Dictionary matches in zxcvbn’s selected match sequence. Dictionary content includes words, names and common passwords; a leet label requires a model-recognized substitution.
INTERPRETATION & PRIVACY

Patterns are observations

Breach occurrences are published source counts, not verified unique people. Repeated occurrences cannot establish cross-site password reuse without account-level evidence.

The source is old, breach-selected, and potentially affected by preprocessing and language bias. It cannot represent everyone’s current password behavior or establish psychological causes.

Python uses zxcvbn 4.5.0; the browser uses the original JavaScript 4.4.2. Scores range from 0 to 4. The displayed offline example assumes 10,000 guesses per second and is an estimate, not a promised cracking time.

The lab scores your example on this device. It computes a SHA-256 digest in memory and compares it with the 1,000 most frequent entries included in this file. Closing the page clears the example.
